body.heading: Shapes are hiding
paragraphs: Shapes are not just in maths books. A clock is a circle. A window is a rectangle. A pizza slice is nearly a triangle.
Write four shapes on your paper: circle, square, triangle, rectangle. Your hunt is to find three of each.

body.heading: Hunt room by room
paragraphs: Start in the kitchen. Plates are circles, tiles are squares, and the fridge door is a tall rectangle.
Triangles are the shyest shape. Look at roof pictures, folded napkins, and the slice lines on a cheese or a cake.

body.heading: Count and crown
paragraphs: Count your finds for each shape. Which shape lives in your home the most? Rectangles usually win — doors, books, screens, and bricks.
Once you start shape hunting, you cannot stop. The whole world is built from shapes pretending to be things.

takeaway: Circles, squares, triangles, and rectangles hide in everyday things, and hunting them changes how you see your home.
safetyNotes: Only hunt in rooms your adult says are fine. Do not touch anything hot, sharp, or breakable.
screenFreeExtension: Draw a picture of your house using only the shapes you found.
